text:
Rina (CEO): Thanks for the questions in today's all-hands. I'm dropping an open thread to capture clarifications about release cadence, oncall, quality bars, and SLAs so leadership can follow up.

Sam (Head of Product): Quick note: product expects clearer gating for API breaking changes vs. non-breaking. Can eng give a short definition we can rely on?

Eva (Director of Reliability): Our working definition: breaking = client-visible schema/contract change or behavior change that can cause incorrect client logic. Anything else is non-breaking. We'll add examples to the runbook.

Luis (Eng Manager): About cadence 1 releases/month target seems tight for teams that own infra + models. Can we scope "major" vs "minor" releases more concretely?

Dylan (SRE): Proposal: major = changes touching model weights, API surface, DB migrations; minor = config, perf tunings, internal infra improvements. Major releases follow 3-week planning cycle, minor releases can be rolled weekly with canary.

Sam (Head of Product): That helps. How do we handle data migrations that are live? Any preflight checks recommended?

Eva (Director of Reliability): Preflight checklist suggestion: 
- migration dry-run in staging; 
- traffic ramp plan with at least 2 rollback points; 
- automated smoke tests that validate critical paths.
We can add a migration template to the releases repo.

Luis (Eng Manager): Oncall rotation question from the team: reduce primary from 3w to 2w to lower burnout, but worried about more frequent handoffs. Any middle ground?

Dylan (SRE): Middle ground: 2w primary + dedicated 1w handover buffer (shadow/overlap). During overlap the outgoing primary stays available for context but not paged first. That reduces knowledge loss while keeping shorter primes.

Rina (CEO): Sounds reasonable to pilot for 2 teams. Which ones?

Luis (Eng Manager): Suggest runtime and api-platform teams as pilot candidates. They have mature playbooks.

Dylan (SRE): I'll prepare a pilot schedule and a simple handoff checklist: incident summary, outstanding tickets, ongoing rollouts, and a link to recent deploys.

Sam (Head of Product): On quality bars: product wants auto-eval alerts to be actionable and not noisy. What thresholds are we comfortable blocking on?

Eva (Director of Reliability): Suggested thresholds: 
- relevance (golden set): block if >4% relative drop; 
- hallucinations: block if >6% absolute increase; 
- perf: block if 95p latency >10% regression.
These are starting points and we'll tune by model family and traffic.

Rina (CEO): Who owns the decision to unfreeze a blocked release? Is it model owner, eng manager, or leadership?

Eva (Director of Reliability): Protocol: model owner must acknowledge within 4 business hours and propose mitigation within 24 hours. If unresolved, the release lead + product manager + reliability lead make a go/no-go within 48 hours. We'll put this in a short escalation flow.

ops-bot: Reminder: incident playbook updated: new oncall overlap template at https://redwood.internal/playbooks/oncall-overlap

Luis (Eng Manager): Action items: I will draft the "major vs minor" checklist, include data migration preflight, and put handover template in the releases repo by next Tuesday.

Dylan (SRE): I'll share the pilot schedule and the oncall overlap runbook PR by EOW. Also adding SLO metrics for API tiers to a PR.

Sam (Head of Product): I'll work with product PMs to classify upcoming changes for the next release so we can practice the gating.

Rina (CEO): Thanks team. I'll expect a one-page summary after the pilot to evaluate. Drop any edge cases here (cross-service releases, infra-only rollouts, hotfixes) so we can add to the runbook. :smile:
